Detailed Description Statement Reference dpy ov1 mutants exhibit epidermal invaginations or elevations on the notum at the muscle insertion sites of DLM (comma phenotype), as well as a oblique wing. ( Chu and Hayashi, 2021 ) dpy ov1 homozygotes show a small, oblique wing phenotype. ( Kandasamy et al., 2021 ) dpy ov1 mutant wing blades exhibit collapse of the distal tip: the 'dumpy' phenotype. dpy o2 / dpy ov1 mutant wing blades exhibit complete retraction of the wing blade: the 'truncate' phenotype. ( Ray et al., 2015 ) Mutant flies show significantly increased survival compared to wild-type flies after infection with E. chaffeensis. Bacterial replication is significantly reduced in the mutant flies compared to wild type. ( Von Ohlen et al., 2012 ) Mutant flies have anterior indentations in the notum epidermis. ( Olguín et al., 2011 ) "ov" class allele. ( Carmon et al., 2010 ) dp ov1 embryos do not show defects in tracheal tube length and do not show breaks in the tracheal branches. ( Swanson et al., 2009 ) dp TC4 / dp ov1 flies have "lopped" and "vortex" phenotypes. Body and leg size are reduced. ( Carlson, 1956 )
